prompt:
Write the appraiser's remarks (about 80 words) on a body shop repair estimate after a low-speed head-on collision. Describe the damage seen on the vehicle and the repair plan. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1458; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- Two similar charges on the same day are being checked.
- The repair labor hours fit the damage.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
text: The vehicle arrived with crushed front bumper cover, cracked grille and a displaced hood latch, with the radiator support showing bending consistent with a frontal impact at low speed. Some of the lower damage may have come from this collision, but it is not yet clear whether all of it did, so the older-looking marks on the lower panels are being checked before final approval. The repair plan calls for replacing the bumper cover, grille, hood latch and radiator support, with refinishing of the front end and a scan for sensor faults. The labor hours listed fit the damage described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known. Two similar charges on the same day are being checked against the file before payment is released.
